title: How BlackRock Builds Custom Knowledge Apps at Scale — Vaibhav Page & Infant Vasanth, BlackRock
talk_summary: BlackRock built a two-part internal framework — a 'sandbox' where domain experts iterate extraction templates, prompts, validations and LLM strategies, and an 'app factory' (cloud-native operator) that turns those definitions into deployed apps — compressing app build time from 3-8 months to a couple of days. They emphasize human-in-the-loop, per-field validation/QC, and ROI checks before building.

takeaways.technique: Per-field extraction templates with validations, QC checks and inter-field dependencies
takeaways.what_they_do: Each extracted field is defined with data type, source (extracted vs derived), required flag, dependencies and validation constraints, so results are checked structurally rather than by eyeballing prompts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I need to have multiple QC checks on the result values. I need to have a lot of validations and constraints on the fields

takeaways.technique: Sandbox for fast prompt/strategy iteration by domain experts
takeaways.what_they_do: They federate the bottleneck (prompt creation, extraction templates, LLM strategy choice, extraction runs) into a self-serve sandbox so the people with domain knowledge iterate without waiting on engineering.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you can get that sandbox out into the hands of the domain experts then your iteration speed becomes really fast
takeaways.numbers: app build time compressed from 3-8 months to a couple of days

takeaways.technique: Strategy selection per document/task, not one global approach
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly choose between in-context, RAG, chain-of-thought etc. per instrument/document size, and mix strategies with prompts, because a single approach fails across cases.
A cloud-native operator takes a declarative definition produced in the sandbox and spins out the deployed app, making deployment as close to CI/CD as possible.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an app factory which is like our cloudnative operator which takes a definition and spins out an app

takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately keep humans in the loop for regulated work rather than going fully agentic, and design the workflow around that check.
takeaways.evidence_quote: design for human in the loop first

takeaways.technique: ROI check before building an AI app
takeaways.what_they_do: They evaluate whether spinning up an AI app is actually cheaper than an off-the-shelf product before committing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: evaluate what your ROI is and as is it going to be like more expensive actually spinning up an AI app versus just having like an offtheshelf product
